title: VST Tillers Tractors Ltd-$ - 531266 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: VST Tillers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2% to INR321.6 crore, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 200 bps to 11% on commodity costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR321.6 crore, up about 2% YoY, while operational EBITDA fell to INR35.1 crore (11%) from INR40.9 crore, which management attributed to commodity-driven material cost inflation over the last two quarters. PAT was INR22.8 crore versus INR25.4 crore a year earlier. For H1, revenue grew 6% to INR635 crore and PAT rose to INR71.5 crore from INR69.9 crore, with operational EBITDA margin at 12% versus 13%. Management said the domestic tractor business is down 4% in H1 on drought in Maharashtra and North Karnataka and expects flat tractor volumes for the full year, while power weeders and tillers are expected to accelerate in H2.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR40.9 crore last year; ~200 bps margin drop
vs 13% last year; ~100 bps drop, all from raw material cost

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Q2 sales 13,357 units (+2% YoY); H1 sales 27,158 units (+9%). Management cited about 11% growth and expects continued growth in H2 on a government order pipeline.

segments.name: Power weeders
segments.commentary: H1 sales 6,076 units (+22%). Management expects H2 acceleration to bring full-year growth to about 40-50%, versus close to 10,000 units last year.

segments.name: Power reapers
segments.commentary: Q2 sales 1,143 units; H1 sales 1,171 units. Season delayed by late monsoon, expected to extend into Q3.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales 940 units; H1 sales 1,925 units, down about 4%. Management expects flat full-year domestic volume, with Maharashtra (about 40% of compact tractor business) and North Karnataka under drought.

segments.name: Tractors (export)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales 226 units; H1 sales 501 units. Netherlands warehouse signed; first shipment expected by end-Q3 and full operations from Q4, with expected flat full-year export volume.

segments.name: Distribution business
segments.commentary: Management said it continues to grow at over 20%.

guidance_outlook: Overall SFM (small farm machinery) business expected to deliver double-digit growth for FY27.
Power weeder growth expected at about 40-50% for FY27, with rear rotary weeders expected to take off in Q1-Q2 of next year after launch.
Tractor domestic volumes expected flat for FY27; Zetor full-size tractors expected to grow about 40-50% YoY, with management declining to give unit numbers.
Export tractor volumes expected to move from negative to flat for FY27 once the Netherlands warehouse operates from Q4.
Working capital (receivables and inventory) expected to ease in Q3 and Q4 per management.
capex_capacity: Dealer network above 800 dealerships and more than 1,000 counters; target of more than 2,000 counters by end of FY27.
Netherlands warehouse to cut delivery lead time to distributors to about 2 weeks from 60-90 days; first lot to ship by end of Q3, operations from Q4.
SCORE platform (between power tiller and tractor) launching Nov-Dec 2026, with about 500 units planned in H2; larger volumes expected in FY28.
4-wheel-drive higher-horsepower tractor due towards end of FY27; new global platform for India, Europe and US to launch in Q4, contributing more in FY28.
Retail tiller financing penetration at about 11-12%, targeted to reach about 15% by year-end (originally 20% target); financing via NBFCs and some banks.
demand_pricing: Maharashtra industry down more than 20% and expected to drop further in Q3 per October industry data; Solapur inquiries falling.
Competitor selling tractors at much lower prices in Gujarat for 2-3 months; management expects this to stop.
Eastern and southern paddy markets (Odisha, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Andhra) have good rainfall; Andhra affected by a recent cyclone.

Company has taken two price hikes in FY27 on both tillers and tractors; further hike under evaluation, with some competitors announcing November hikes. Management may wait about two weeks as crude prices have eased.

Inventory rose by about INR43 crore and receivables by about INR40 crore; payables rose about INR55 crore. Management called the rise temporary, linked to TREM V emission norm change and commodity purchases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor business going flat when launches were expected to drive growth, and what about northern expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said north growth is real but cannot offset the Maharashtra drop of more than 20%; Maharashtra is about 40% of the compact tractor business, concentrated in pomegranate and grape orchards.

qa_highlights.question: Will SCORE cannibalise tiller sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SCORE targets dry markets such as sugarcane and orchards where tillers are weak, at a price close to a tiller, and that about 500 units are planned for H2.

qa_highlights.question: What supports the H2 tractor recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Zetor expected to grow 40-50%, and Phantom series growth in non-drought markets is expected to offset the 4-5% H1 decline. No unit numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in receivables and inventory a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the receivables rise is temporary and will come down in Q3-Q4, and that the inventory build reflects TREM V changes and commodity purchases.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to protect gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating a price hike and may wait about two weeks because crude prices have fallen sharply; it would revisit pricing if commodity inflation persists.

risks_watch: Operational EBITDA margin pressure from commodity inflation; further price hikes not yet decided.
Maharashtra and North Karnataka drought, with expected further Q3 decline in the tractor industry.
Competitor price cuts in Gujarat; management expects them to end but this is unconfirmed.
Working capital build (inventory +INR43 crore, receivables +INR40 crore) must unwind in Q3-Q4 as management guided.
Execution risk on the Netherlands warehouse, SCORE ramp, and rear rotary weeder launches.
summary.management_tone: Confident on tillers, power weeders and distribution growth, but cautious on tractors, where management has cut its outlook to flat and acknowledged the Maharashtra drought impact. Management was less specific on margins and pricing, saying it was still evaluating a price hike, and declined to give Zetor unit numbers.

SCORE platform (between power tiller and tractor) launch Nov-Dec 2026, ~500 units planned in H2
4-wheel-drive higher-horsepower tractor due towards end of FY27; new global platform launch in Q4, contributing more in FY28

growth.why: Management guides domestic tractors flat for FY27 (cut), power weeders ~40% and SFM double-digit growth, with Zetor full-size up 40-50%; backing is partial via dealer counters, Netherlands warehouse, SCORE launch and price hikes, but no unit or capacity numbers for the bulk of the growth, while domestic tractor and Maharashtra demand are weakening.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operational EBITDA margin fell about 200 bps to 11% in Q2 (INR35.1 crore vs INR40.9 crore) on commodity inflation over two quarters, and H1 margin is 12% vs 13%; the only offset is a possible price hike still under evaluation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Netherlands warehouse first shipment by end-Q3 with full operations from Q4, dealer counters targeted to rise from 1,000+ to more than 2,000 by end FY27, and SCORE launching Nov-Dec 2026 with about 500 units in H2; these are distribution and product capacity, not plant capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Power weeders H1 up 22% to 6,076 units with guidance of about 40-50% full-year growth, power tillers H1 up 9% with continued H2 growth, and Zetor expected up 40-50%; offset by domestic tractors down about 4% in H1 and flat full-year guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed on the call and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Domestic tractor volume guidance was cut to flat for FY27, the Maharashtra industry is down more than 20% and expected to fall further in Q3, and retail finance penetration target was cut from 20% to about 15%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tractor guidance was already cut to flat and management expects a further Q3 drop in Maharashtra; the margin trend is down 200 bps in Q2 and the price hike is undecided, so the risk of further cuts is real but not confirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SCORE platform launch in Nov-Dec 2026 with about 500 units in H2, rear rotary weeders expected to take off after launch, and a 4-wheel-drive tractor and new global platform due in Q4 FY27 contributing more in FY28.

rows.label: Working capital unwind in Q3-Q4
rows.why: Inventory rose about INR43 crore and receivables about INR40 crore in H1; management guided both to ease in Q3 and Q4, though the unwind is not yet proven.

rows.label: Further price hike under evaluation
rows.why: Two price hikes already taken in FY27 and competitors announcing November hikes, but management may wait about two weeks as crude has eased, so no decision yet to protect the 200 bps margin drop.

rows.label: Government order pipeline for power tillers
rows.why: Management expects continued power tiller growth in H2 on a government order pipeline; Q2 power tiller units were up only 2% YoY at 13,357 units, so the pipeline is not yet converting strongly.

tone.note: Management was confident on power weeders, tillers and distribution (over 20% growth) but cautious on domestic tractors after the Maharashtra drought and vague on margins and the pending price hike; analysts pushed on why tractor launches are not offsetting the drought and on the working capital bui
